reason: Real but much narrower than stated. The global handler does emit str(exc) as a raw 502 detail (app.py:312-315) and unclassified ProviderErrors leak internals (the /quotes/ZZZQNOPE repro reproduces verbatim), and no failure message carries a 'what would unlock it'. But the claim that three panels print that string does not hold for this repro: /fundamentals already maps not_found/rate_limited to human 404/429 text (fundamentals.py:~103-114, live 404 'No instrument matches ... check the symbol.'); Watchlist uses batch /quotes, which silently drops a failed symbol (200, row gets a null quote, watchlist/api.ts:37-41); Chart's /history returns 200 with empty bars and reason 'in_eod_only'; Equity Overview uses allSettled and on all-failed shows 'No data available for X' (EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:754-756), so the catch at :763 is effectively unreachable. The leak remains only for unclassified (kind=None) errors: the single-symbol /quotes route, the fundamentals 502 fall-through (fundamentals.py:115 -> EmptyState hint at EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:1048), and the chart catch at ChartPanel.tsx:408. Secondary defect: a nonexistent symbol on /quotes/{symbol} is misclassified as an unclassified yfinance attribute error instead of not_found. Downgraded to low because common failures are already humanized and the remaining leak is a polish and edge case.

reason: Holds. PortfolioPanel fetches quotes and badges only a rejected fetch (setQuotesError, PortfolioPanel.tsx:141-160). reason: Holds. On a native-search tier, the runtime sets opts web_search=True with web_search_max_uses=5 and strips the local web_search tool (agent_runtime.py:1335-1340). OpenAI/xAI/OpenRouter, Gemini and Groq adapters pop web_search_max_uses unused (openai.py:665-667, gemini.py:112, groq.py:117), and only Anthropic applies it, per request. The only loop counter (web_search_calls, agent_runtime.py:1416,1553-1556) increments on local 'web_search' tool calls, which are absent on that tier. This contradicts the native_search.py:109-113 docstring that promises a loop-level counter. No native-search usage is metered anywhere (grep for server_tool_use/web_search_requests/search_count finds nothing), and BudgetGuard prices tokens only (budget_guard.py:82-84), so per-search charges are invisible to the spend ceiling.
evidence_checked: Code-only (an LLM-backed repro would cost spend and is not needed). Opened the runtime, all adapter pop sites, the native_search helpers and budget_guard, and grepped for any native-search metering.
repro_check: grep -rn 'web_search_max_uses' sidecar/services/llm -> popped and discarded in openai/gemini/groq, used only in anthropic; grep for server_tool_use|web_search_requests|search_count in the runtime/adapters/budget_guard -> no matches.

reason: Holds. In the registry, only openbb-mcp (rank 10) and yfinance (rank 50) serve fundamentals, income_statement, balance_sheet, cash_flow and analyst_rating. The IN-scoped providers nse_direct, nse and bse serve quote and ohlcv only, and the code comments say 'IN fundamentals fall through to yfinance'. A live GET /fundamentals/RELIANCE.NS on :52152 returns provider='yfinance'. That contradicts spec.md:817 ('yfinance is never the trusted India primary'). D72 documents openbb's all-null IN shells, so yfinance is in practice the primary for the numbers shown.
evidence_checked: Opened the registry declarations, the fundamentals router and the spec clause; ran a live GET against :52152.
repro_check: curl :52152/fundamentals/RELIANCE.NS -> provider='yfinance', market_cap=16785679056896.0, pe_ratio=22.45 (yfinance is the serving primary for an IN large-cap).
